headline: High-risk data exfiltration and cascading-error pathway: Firecrawl’s broad egress can carry sensitive web/API content while the AI-engineering-hub side offers no isolation or verification controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API surfaces, so attacker-controlled pages can reach its outputs. ai-engineering-hub is an MCP/agents repository with no documented isolation or provenance controls, so a shared channel is plausible. The pairwise injection path is inferred, not directly documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is copied into an agent prompt or MCP message without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF ai-engineering-hub components parse external content as instructions, attacker text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of scraped text into prompts.
Add a fixed instruction/content delimiter in the handoff format.
Strip HTML, markdown links, and code fences before passing content.
Review one sample Firecrawl output for prompt-injection markers.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and content-type validation at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl explicitly touches web content, structured data, screenshots, and API keys, and it has broad network egress. ai-engineering-hub is docs-only with no stated data classes, but its agent/MCP orientation means the pair can move sensitive content through Firecrawl’s backend. The shared-workspace path is not shown, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF API keys or screenshots are sent through Firecrawl, they may leave the local environment.
IF ai-engineering-hub workflows forward scraped content into Firecrawl requests, that content can be transmitted to a third party.
mitigations: Avoid sending secrets or screenshots to Firecrawl.
Use a redaction step before any Firecrawl call.
Rotate any API key used in testing.
Limit Firecrawl jobs to non-sensitive domains.
requires-engineering: enforce per-field allowlists on outbound payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl supports multiple instances and broad API/CLI use, while ai-engineering-hub is an agents/MCP repository that may orchestrate writes or network actions. Overlapping mutable-resource access is plausible, but no shared filesystem or git-write capability is documented for either side, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or git checkout, concurrent edits can collide.
IF an orchestrator launches multiple Firecrawl instances against shared state, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate working directory.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Avoid concurrent git operations during scraping.
Check for stale files before overwriting.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data that downstream agents may treat as facts. ai-engineering-hub is an agents/RAG/MCP repository, so the pair plausibly creates an A-to-B handoff with no documented verification step. Because Firecrawl can feed untrusted content into downstream actions, the blast radius can include incorrect or unsafe actions, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is used as authoritative input to another agent, errors can cascade.
IF the downstream agent acts on scraped facts without verification, it can commit or communicate incorrect information.
mitigations: Require a human review step for high-impact outputs.
Compare scraped facts against a second source before acting.
Mark Firecrawl output as untrusted in prompts.
Log source URLs alongside extracted claims.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking and confidence gating.

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys, and its broad egress can move regulated data off-platform. ai-engineering-hub has no documented residency, retention, or certification controls, so the pair creates a compliance gap by default. The evidence is indirect, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF EU personal data or secrets are processed through Firecrawl, they may leave the intended jurisdiction.
IF the operator relies on ai-engineering-hub for retention or deletion controls, those controls are not documented here.
mitigations: Do not process regulated data through Firecrawl.
Confirm a DPA and residency terms before use.
Set a short retention window for logs.
Delete test artifacts after validation.
requires-engineering: implement jurisdiction-aware routing and retention enforcement.
